north_star.title: Personal knowledge base
north_star.problem_statement: Notes are scattered across tools and hard to revisit.
north_star.desired_outcome: One place to capture and resurface ideas.
success_criteria: Can find a note from 6 months ago in under a minute
north_star.current_hypothesis: A local-first app with full-text search is enough.
north_star.next_action: Prototype a search index over existing notes.

proposal.statement: Build the local-first desktop app first; defer the browser clipper.
proposal.rationale: It directly answers the core problem and has the fewest unknowns.
alternatives_considered: Lead with the browser extension clipper

branches.name: Local-first app
branches.summary: SQLite-backed desktop app with full-text search.

branches.name: Browser extension clipper
branches.summary: Capture web pages into the same store.
branches.revisit_trigger: After the core search flow works.

assumptions.statement: Users will trust a local-only store without cloud backup.
assumptions.falsifying_evidence: A user loses notes to a disk failure and churns.

assumptions.statement: Full-text search is the primary way notes get resurfaced.

evidence.claim: SQLite FTS5 handles 50k notes with sub-100ms search.
evidence.notes: Confirmed in the docs' performance notes.

evidence.claim: Most notes are never revisited after a week.
evidence.notes: Based on personal recollection, not measured.

research_tasks.question: How do comparable local-first note apps handle backup and recovery?
Can SQLite FTS5 scale to the note volume we expect?

decisions.question: Sync between devices or single-device only?
decisions.rationale: Sync adds conflict-resolution complexity not worth it yet.

next_actions.description: Prototype SQLite FTS5 search over 100 sample notes.
next_actions.success_signal: Search returns relevant results in under a second.
next_actions.failure_signal: Setup takes more than a day.

open_questions: Should tags be freeform or structured?
